messages:
Chris: FYI noticed a persistent GPU resident growth on nightly long-run perf test. OOMs on gpu-7 after ~8h, even though request rate is steady. Dumped a couple profiler snapshots + nvml logs.

Chris: Early hypothesis: either fragmentation from our allocator or KV cache not evicting prefixes properly when batch sizes spike. Also saw a spike in workspace allocations during kernel selection changes.

Chris: Paste of the OOM trace we get (trimmed):
```
[2026-05-12T03:21:17Z] ERROR runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
  at runtime/cuda/alloc.cc:214
  allocate_workspace(seq=4096, bs=8) -> trying 1.2GB
  allocator: slab_resident=22.1GB, slab_free=1.2GB
  kvcache: entries=13k, resident=4.8GB
  pinned_buffers: 312MB
```

Lina: Ack. Can you share the profiler snapshots + exact repro command? I can run a bisection on kernel-picker if it's related.

Chris: Repro command I used on staging (fast loop):
```bash
python tools/repro/gpu_drift_repro.py --model vicuna-13b --iters 12000 --batch 8 --seq 4096 --kv-policy=none
```
It reliably produces resident growth after ~6-9h. I also tested with --batch 1 and growth is much slower.

Maria: Interesting that smaller batch slows it. Could be batching heuristic causing many long sequences to coalesce and blow KV cache + workspace. Did you run with kernel selection debug on?

Chris: Yes, with env DEBUG_KERNELS=1. Noticed the kernel picker switches from fused-attn to stable-fwd for some layers mid-run (due to sequence length distribution change). When that flips, workspace size jumps and a bunch of temporary buffers are allocated.

Sam: That flipping could create transient buffer churn. If allocator reuses buffers by shape sign, and we pick kernels that request slightly different alignment, we may be leaking aligned fragments (fragmentation) instead of a logical leak.

AJ: Also worth checking KV cache eviction: our policy uses passive eviction based on recent access + resident threshold. If batching increases prefix reuse, we may pin more keys. Can you dump kv cache LRU tail?

Chris: I attached two artifacts in the staging job: profiler snapshots s3://redwood-perf/gpu-drift/1769987654/{snap1,snap2}.nvprof and nvml CSV s3://redwood-perf/gpu-drift/1769987654/nvml.csv. Quick grep showed kv.cache.resident_bytes rising steadily between snaps (~400MB -> 1.9GB).

Lina: I'll pull them. If kv.resident grows but total allocated memory doesn't free, that's a real retention issue. If total allocated stays constant but free fragmentation increases, that's fragmentation. We need both the allocator histogram and the KV index snapshot.

Chris: Alloc hist (from allocator_stats endpoint):
```
size_bucket: 64KB count=2000
size_bucket: 256KB count=1200
size_bucket: 1MB   count=400   <- increased between snaps
workspace_alloc_count: +240
```
Shows 1MB bucket grew a lot.

Sam: 1MB bump aligns with workspace blowup from the kernel flip. Could be we allocate many 1MB temporary buffers and they aren't returned to the freelist because of a bug in free path when workspace id != allocated slab id (race with concurrent batch flush).

Maria: Repro strategy: 1) isolate kernel flip by forcing a single kernel codepath for entire run (env KERNEL_FORCE=fused-attn), 2) run with kv eviction forced (KV_EVICT_IMMEDIATE=1), 3) run with allocator debug mode to log frees (ALLOC_DEBUG_FREE=1). Compare mem trajectories.

Chris: I ran 1) forcing fused-attn: growth rate drops ~4x, still some drift but no OOM at 8h. 2) with KV_EVICT_IMMEDIATE=1 growth stops almost entirely. 3) ALLOC_DEBUG_FREE logs show some frees failing with "free: slab mismatch" intermittently.

AJ: "slab mismatch" is alarming. Could be allocator metadata overwrite or handle reuse bug. Do we have a minimal repro that triggers free consistently?

Chris: I made a smaller bisection script that toggles kernel selection at runtime to force the pattern: tools/repro/kernel_flip_bisect.py. It toggles kernel choice every N batches and replays the same request traces. With flip interval=256 it reproduces the free failures within ~2000 iterations.

Lina: Great. Can you open a PR with the repro and link to the two nvprof snaps + allocator logs? I can run address-sanitizer build on that repro and check metadata writes.

Sam: Workarounds we can ship quickly: - enforce single kernel per model until allocator fix landed - reduce max_batch_tokens to limit stash size - force more aggressive KV eviction for Dedicated customers w/ high sequence variance.

Maria: Long term fixes: - tighten allocator free path to validate slab ids and drop silent failures - improve workspace sizing tolerance to avoid minor kernel alignment differences causing new allocations - add a periodic compact pass that coalesces small freed runs into larger chunks for fragmentation relief.

Chris: I'm opening a tracking issue with a summary + artifacts: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-1456. I'll attach the repro script and a minimal bisection harness.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: canary env c2 -> staging tomorrow 09:00 UTC with kernel pin feature flag.

Lina: I'll run ASAN + fsanitize on the repro in the morning and share a debug build. If we get a consistent free mismatch we can make a tiny guard check to fail fast and log metadata to root cause.

AJ: If anyone needs quick metrics, add this to your staging job: --metric-sinks=kv_lru_tail,allocator_hist,workspace_active. Those helped earlier to correlate events.

Chris: Thanks all. Next actions: Lina runs ASAN, Maria drafts allocator fix plan, Sam prepares kernel-pin rollout, AJ looks at KV eviction thresholds. I'll post updates in this thread and upload any new traces to s3 path above. :thumbsup:

Lina: copying @Maria @Sam for visibility.

Maria: grabbing the artifacts now.

Sam: will prep a canary checklist.

Chris: closing loop — added small patch to log slab ids on free in staging PR #4567. If that shows missing slab ids we'll have a smoking gun.
